script: Your dog is lying there, and suddenly their whole body jerks with a little hic. It looks odd, but dog hiccups are usually harmless and very common, especially in puppies. They happen when the diaphragm, the muscle under the lungs, contracts in sudden spasms, and the voice box closes with that familiar hic sound. The most common triggers are eating or drinking too fast, excitement, play, and swallowing air. Puppies get them more often because their bodies are still developing. So how do you stop them? First, stay calm, because most episodes pass on their own within a few minutes. Offering a little water can help relax the diaphragm, and a gentle belly rub or a slow, quiet walk can settle their breathing. If your dog gulps their food, a slow feeder bowl or smaller meals can prevent a lot of hiccups. Skip the old myth about scaring your dog, because it doesn't help. Call your vet if the hiccups last more than a few hours, happen often, or come with coughing, wheezing, vomiting or trouble breathing. Otherwise, think of them as a harmless quirk, and a sign your dog just ate a little too fast.
